entries.title: Jeremiah 26:11
segments: God's faithful servants generally receive the bitterest persecution from false and corrupt religious teachers.

entries.title: Jeremiah 26:14
segments: The true messenger of God will commit his cause to his divine Master, and prefer death rather than unfaithfulness.

entries.title: Jeremiah 26:15
segments: God regards the injury which his servants receive for the truth's sake as done to himself, and he will punish it accordingly.

entries.title: Jeremiah 26:16
segments:
vv 16-19. 
 
True nobleness of character is shown by listening to faithful reproofs and profiting by them; to hate and persecute those who administer them betrays equal baseness and wickedness.

entries.title: Jeremiah 26:19
segments: Did Hezekiah--put him at all to death? this case is adduced by the princes as an argument why the king should spare Jeremiah.

entries.title: Jeremiah 26:20
segments:
Urijah; this case is adduced by the prophet to show the disposition of Jehoiakim, and the danger to which he was exposed. 
 
vv 20-23. 
 
To show fear of wicked men who are high in office and power, is oftentimes the most certain way to give them the mastery over us.

entries.title: Jeremiah 26:24
segments: It is easy for God to raise up friends and protectors for the defenceless, and he will do so for those who put their trust in him, as far as their good and the interests of his cause demand it.
